skill.name: dx-optimizer
skill.description: Developer Experience specialist. Improves tooling, setup, and workflows. Use PROACTIVELY when setting up new projects, after team feedback, or when development friction is noticed.
skill.summary: Improves setup, tooling, automation, documentation, and feedback loops for developer workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged three Markdown inline-code references as Ruby or shell backtick execution. All three are false positives because SKILL.md contains prose instructions and does not execute commands or interpolate user input.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 is a Markdown inline-code reference in documentation, not Ruby or shell execution. SKILL.md is prose-only and contains no executable backtick command context.
Line 68 is a Markdown bullet naming command additions as a deliverable. It is not code execution and does not contain a command injection path.
Line 69 is a Markdown bullet naming project scripts as a deliverable. It is descriptive prose, not a shell invocation or Ruby backtick execution.

content.value_statement: Development teams lose time to slow setup, unclear tooling, and repeated manual tasks. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code identify friction and propose practical workflow improvements.
actual_capabilities: Profiles current developer workflows to find setup, build, test, and documentation friction.
Recommends incremental improvements for dependency setup, task automation, and feedback loops.
Plans deliverables such as command shortcuts, package scripts, git hooks, IDE settings, and README updates.
Defines success metrics for clone-to-run time, manual steps removed, test speed, and developer feedback.
Creates actionable checklists for onboarding, troubleshooting, and project-specific tooling.
limitations: Does not validate changes against every local machine or operating system without project testing.
Does not replace security review for scripts, hooks, or automation that can execute commands.
Depends on accurate details about the project stack, team workflow, and current pain points.
References an optional playbook path, but this package only includes SKILL.md.

use_cases.title: Improve New Project Onboarding
use_cases.description: Create a short setup flow with clear defaults, reliable commands, and troubleshooting notes.

use_cases.title: Reduce Repetitive Local Tasks
use_cases.description: Identify repeated manual work and convert it into maintainable scripts, aliases, or task runner commands.

use_cases.title: Speed Up Feedback Loops
use_cases.description: Review build, test, and hot reload workflows, then propose measurable improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dx-optimizer skill to review this project setup. Identify the top developer friction points and suggest simple improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a broad DX review

prompt_templates.title: Create an Onboarding Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dx-optimizer skill to create a clone-to-running checklist for this repository. Include required tools, common failures, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Workflow Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dx-optimizer skill to find repeated manual tasks in our workflow. Recommend scripts, shortcuts, git hooks, or IDE settings that reduce effort.
prompt_templates.scenario: Automation planning for an active team

prompt_templates.title: Measure DX Improvements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dx-optimizer skill to build a DX improvement plan with baseline metrics, incremental changes, validation steps, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Review our setup process and make onboarding faster.
output: A ranked list of setup blockers and repeated manual steps.
A proposed onboarding checklist with verification commands described in prose.
Success metrics for time to first successful local run.

output_examples.input: Our tests and builds feel slow during feature work.
output: A workflow profile covering build, test, and reload delays.
Incremental improvements for faster local feedback.
Measurement steps for comparing before and after results.

output_examples.input: Help standardize our team development tooling.
output: Recommended IDE settings, command shortcuts, and documentation updates.
Suggested ownership for keeping tooling current.
Checks to confirm the changes work across the team.

best_practices: Start with current workflow evidence before proposing automation.
Make each tooling change small, reversible, and easy to validate.
Measure setup time, manual steps, and feedback-loop speed after changes.
anti_patterns: Adding scripts or hooks without explaining what they do and how to disable them.
Optimizing uncommon tasks while ignoring daily build, test, and setup friction.
Assuming one developer machine represents every team environment.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It focuses on setup, local tooling, repetitive workflows, feedback loops, and developer-facing documentation.

faq.question: Can it change project files automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest or help implement changes when the agent has file access and user approval.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: The skill text does not run commands. Any command execution depends on the host agent and user permissions.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can profile current friction and recommend incremental improvements for established repositories.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the project stack, current setup steps, frequent pain points, and any constraints for scripts or tools.
